name: K-State TRIGA Mark III hot element, 1.25 MW, 20 C pool, SAR film coefficient (eq. 7)
label: sourced
citation: As the K-State hot-element case (radii Table 4.6, k Tables 13.3 and 4.6, gap conductance Appendix A, q' from eq. 9 at 1.25 MW), except the boundary: pool water at 20 C (Table 4.8) and the convective coefficient h = 0.0326 P + 16985 W/m2/K with P the reactor power in watts (SAR section 4.5.3, eq. 7 and Figure 4.10, a linear fit of values the SAR calculated between 500 and 1900 kW) = 57735 W/m2/K at 1.25 MW. Read from the page image: the printed trendline in Figure 4.10 is y = 0.0326x + 16985 and the plotted points (about 33000 W/m2/K at 500 kW to about 78000 at 1900 kW) fit it only with P in watts.
description: The K-State 1.25 MW hottest-element analysis with the SAR's own film coefficient instead of a prescribed wall temperature. Valid for the K-State reference core between 500 and 1900 kW only (the fit range); do not use it for another reactor or power. Source inconsistency: with eq. 7 the film drop is about 9 K and the centreline about 511 C, whereas SAR Table 4.8 implies a film drop of only 1.2 K (wall 21.2 C) and 503.2 C; the SAR does not reconcile them, so this case is checked against the SAR's eq. 9 and not against Table 4.8. A conservative analysis point, not a measured normal operating state. Solid-cylinder model with the zirconium rod ignored, one axial slice at the maximum heat flux. Thermal only.

thermal.conductivity.source: K-State SAR 2004 Table 13.3 (18 W/m/K, all temperatures); UT-Austin SAR 2023 Table 4.1 (0.18 W/cm/K)
K-State SAR 2004 Table 13.3 and Table 4.6 (16.6 W/m/K at 400 K)
